articles.abstract:
The available sources are heterogeneous: queries, search results, memory, instructions, tools, Policy, and model assumptions together form the available context, yet they do not automatically determine which task-specific semantic commitment has been selected, how it was issued, what realizes it, or whether a particular action is permitted.

The central contribution is Meaning Management as an architectural layer governing the lifecycle of task-specific semantic commitments. The selection is fixed by a Resolution Receipt; the Knowledge Contract is separated from issuance; post-issuance Binding is separated from the current Authorization. Variant A, the BKG, the Resolver, the identity model, Expansion/Evolution, and the execution gate formally specify the mechanisms that support this decomposition.

The surveyed purposive corpus covers prompting, retrieval, memory, orchestration, provenance, workflows, policy evaluation, and knowledge representation individually, but provides no single model of this governed transition; the finding is bounded by the corpus and asserts no historical priority. Practical usefulness is tested by nine hypotheses and nine protocols, HYP/EXP-001–009. The experiments have not been run, so error reduction, improved diagnosis, and acceptable cost are not demonstrated.
articles.description: A conceptual architecture that separates available context, selected semantic commitments, the immutable Knowledge Contract, runtime binding, and the authorization of a particular action.
articles.status:
The Status of This Publication

Research 17 — Russian Semantic Source v1 Frozen. The canonical Russian version of the conceptual architecture and the preregistration specification. Empirical validation of the architecture has not yet been performed.

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22013923 — the English preprint is deposited in Zenodo (CERN) under CC BY 4.0. Please cite the DOI.

This status does not imply a finished implementation, a proven superiority, or production readiness. This English text is a translation of the frozen Russian source through the shared Arcanada glossary, not an independent academic rewrite.
articles.title: Meaning Management in Autonomous AI Systems: the Knowledge Contract Architecture

articles.abstract:
Systems of cooperating LLM agents exchange state as prose. Prose handoffs lose deontic force, invert relation directions, invite readers to fill gaps with defaults, and leave a knowledge store’s internal wholeness uncheckable. We present a knowledge substrate in which the unit of exchange is a context — a finite set of typed, scoped assertions under a snapshot pin — carried on immutable, digest-pinned, append-only revisions, with every algebraic law of the transfer operations proved or refuted on this carrier rather than assumed. The substrate is implemented and mutation-tested — a refusal catalog of 27 codes at the 2026-08-30 evidence pin, each proven red and growing since only through that same door (§8.10); sixteen invariants enforced at honestly labeled tiers; the reduction ladder R0–R3 with exactness certificates — and exercised on real work: a live store grown from 14 to 134 revisions at the §8.10 recount — organic dogfooding for the first stretch, then a bulk corpus lift (14→63, §8.8) and requirements work this paper does not describe (63→134, §8.10), named as what each stretch was rather than folded under one word (an adversarial review, 2026-09-09, found “dogfooding” over-general for growth this paper’s own §8.8/§8.10 attribute to two other causes) — an admission gate 4-for-4 on real tasks, two write races decided by the append-only law, and two contour defects the run itself surfaced — a truncating renderer and an ungoverned executor over-claim. The work refutes three of this line’s own claims — two facets of the token-economy claim and one store-debt figure, the last felled by the parallel run rather than the evaluation — and narrows the delta claim; the refutations are the headline result. On a stage-snapshot-dominated corpus — session-to-session handoffs, where the pilot’s largest reductions (43.1%, 36.4%) lived, are excluded from the systematic sample and untested here — automated spec-only encoding inflates tokens 7.6% across 18 samples, while a structured-summary baseline under the same instruction reaches 14.8% losslessly on the same sources: reduction tracks the encoder, not the format, on this frame. Hand encoding lands within 0.1 percentage points of the pilot’s 38% on a 4-sample subset where the automated arm reduces only 2.2% — a single-point match against a pilot whose own per-artifact spread is about 12 points, stated as what it is rather than as reproduction. Recall of load-bearing source units — not fidelity in the full sense; this measure counts survival of what the source stated and cannot see a fabricated addition (§1.1’s second failure class), a limit an adversarial review found unstated (2026-09-09) — measured jointly: automated packets preserve 99.3% of 437 semantic units, but the hand encoding behind the 38% preserved only 82.7% — the token win and the completeness rule trade against each other, and token-matched compression across formats remains unmeasured. The delta claim narrows to within-task chains (4/4 counter-pairs); at near-lossless encoding, 144 blind downstream grades hit a 47/48 ceiling in every arm alike — no test with that little variance has the power to distinguish packet from honest prose, and none is claimed to. What the typed carrier exhibits, uncompared (an adversarial review, 2026-09-09, found “demonstrably earns” overstated — §8.7 item 4): machine-checkable recall of load-bearing source units after the fact — an observed MUST→SHOULD drift caught by the evaluation’s unit audit, checkable because modality is a field, and not a fidelity claim in the sense that would also catch a fabricated addition — admission gating, digest-decided concurrency, and projection focus. The co-evolution objection — that the corpus and its enforcing checks were built together — has two measured limits. A sensitivity replay, run in the store’s own append-only order, finds pre-enforcement source content for 10 of the 15 discriminable refusal codes; for the other 5 the objection stands, tested and unrefuted. A separate check-removal experiment finds three codes whose suppression admits a revision that subsequently crashes the unchanged Markdown renderer, with no pre-enforcement source witness for those three. This establishes necessity for that operation on those inputs, not independence of the corpus or failure of downstream LLM work. For the algebraic laws of §4 and the invariants of §5 the objection is untested — none of Theorem 1, Proposition 5, I4 or I5 is among the 26 codes the earlier 86-code sensitivity replay reached (§8.7 item 9); membership in the current replay’s 31 witnessed codes was not re-checked. What the design is not compared against is named to the same standard rather than conceded in a phrase: retrieval-augmented handoff, standard graph serializations under shape validation, and token-matched baselines are unmeasured, each carrying the result that would falsify the design. The method itself is adapted rather than invented — specification mutation and vacuity detection, credited in §2.10, where the analogy to weak-versus-strong mutation is withdrawn as wrong. A measurement instrument fabricated a number twice; only recomputation-from-source in CI held.

What this paper is for, stated so it can be quoted against us: it reports what a typed, digest-pinned substrate for inter-agent knowledge transfer exhibits, uncompared — and the measured answer is refusal, not economy.
articles.description: The second version of the Knowledge Contract work: the typed substrate implemented and mutation-tested, its algebraic laws proved or refuted on the carrier, and the empirical check version 1 declared missing — with the refutations as the headline result.

articles.title: Knowledge Contracts, Version 2: A Typed Substrate for Inter-Agent Knowledge Transfer, with Its Algebraic Laws Proved or Refuted

records.title: Foundations of Meaning and Knowledge Management
records.summary: The paper proposes an operational research programme for managing transitions between a source, a representation of its content, a bounded context and the result of applying it. Its main question is when a person or an agent can reuse previously expressed content while keeping essential differences, grounds and limits under a finite budget of attention, memory and computation. The main text offers context-sufficiency boundaries, conditional properties of composition and a refutation programme. Cooking, navigation and circuit design serve synthetic analyses and limited three-book observations, not transfer to other texts. Executed appendix runs are limited and do not establish extraction quality.

records.title: Semantic Objects, Sources and Verifiable Extraction
records.titleRu: Смысловые объекты, источники и проверяемое извлечение
records.summary: The paper proposes a profile of the semantic object (`MeaningObject`) and a protocol for verifiable extraction. The profile ties content to specific source editions, operator scopes, composite grounds, alternative readings and separate assessments. The central hypothesis is that such binding can reduce reuse errors in declared task classes; it admits a negative result, since for plain retrieval detailed markup may cost more than it helps. The main edition prepared a model, a protocol, limited example records and a test design, and ran no automatic extraction on full books. The appendix keeps limited executed slices over structured material, which do not establish extraction from free text.

records.title: Context, Depth and Conditions of Applicability
records.summary: The paper proposes a model in which extracted content, the conditions for understanding it and the conditions of a new application are addressed separately. For each task a finite set of requirements is formed, and applicability is judged against knowledge editions, contexts, the addressee, the method and available grounds. The main edition gives definitions, conditional properties and a test plan and ran no three-book tests; the appendix keeps later limited runs, including a negative result.

records.title: Transformations, Composition and Bounded Transfer
records.summary: Reusing knowledge requires transformations: normalisation, reduction, joining sources, inference, parametrisation and transfer to a new situation. The paper proposes a transition contract linking input editions, the permitted effect, preconditions, postconditions, protected properties, assumptions, losses and the actual output. Geometric similarity only selects candidates. Conditional properties are arguments under explicit premises, and hypotheses about the benefit of the profile are untested; the appendix keeps limited executed experiments that do not confirm them. It does not claim a universal computable algebra of human meaning.

records.title: Query, Retrieval and Verifiable Coverage
records.summary: The paper proposes a profile for moving from a human or agent query to a bounded answer set with checkable grounds. It separates relevance, support, search completeness and applicability. It links a query plan (`QueryPlan`), a candidate set, three separately addressed coverage reports (`CoverageReport`), pinned sources and stop rules. It allows a useful partial answer and does not treat "nothing found" as "nothing known". Its properties hold only under explicit premises: a finite domain, a query parsed in advance, and author-marked metadata. Only an authored finite model was executed; no real-book search has been run.

records.title: Context Composition under a Limited Budget
records.summary: The paper studies how to compose a context from a fixed set of candidates under limited resources. It proposes a conditional model in which requirements, joint grounds, mandatory dependencies, permitted transformations and the actual representation form one object of verification. The main result is a specification, conditional properties, counter-models, a finite executable model and a comparison plan. Executed: 101 finite checks and 17 API probes. Empirical advantage on real books, people, models or products is not established.

records.title: Dialogue, Learning and Alignment of Understanding
records.summary: The paper offers a specification and a limited transition profile over structured dialogue events. It assesses separately how an utterance is interpreted, whether a state transition is admissible, and whether the reply was useful. Interpretation, the subject registry and subject-verification data come from outside the profile. Free-language understanding, real external effects and training of model weights are not claimed. The executed result is a local pilot on fictional, deliberately constructed episodes, without human participants. It matched declared expectations in 31 of 32 episodes on the first run, and a simple baseline reached the same counts on the shared subset, so no advantage was observed.

records.title: Reasoning, Justification and Revision of Conclusions
records.summary: The paper concerns revising a stored conclusion when one of its premises changes. Its central counterexample: a mark "source changed" does not show that a claim is false, since the old justification may be outdated, other support may remain, an opposite premise may be confirmed, or data may be insufficient. The executable profile covers structured claims and declared rules only. A check on real acquired sources has its own scope and does not measure OCR quality, language understanding or industrial agents. The executed basis is an authored finite check on three public documents.

records.title: Documents, Representations and Long-Term Memory
records.summary: The paper treats a document as a defined representation of knowledge for a purpose, audience and genre, and asks what editing and memory must preserve: conditions of applicability, dependent paragraphs, source locators and current permission to use. It separates three levels of result: a specification of obligations, a finite local execution over trusted, already interpreted units, and future empirical work. The execution checks declared dependencies, current admission and the actual Markdown/JSON projection. It does not check whether a quotation matches its primary source or whether the markup is true.

records.title: Knowledge Contract v3: Synthesis of the General Model and a Professional Profile
records.titleRu: Контракт знаний v3: синтез общей модели и профессиональный профиль
records.summary: The paper proposes a general Knowledge Contract (KC) v3 interface linking addressable content to purpose, conditions, grounds, dependencies and rules of use. Nine core groups are extended by six selective profiles. The professional profile separates a unit of work (`WorkItem`), role (`Role`), skill description (`Skill`), solution scheme (`Blueprint`), executor capability, current authority, attempt and evidence. For a bounded interchange format the authors implemented a JSON Schema, consistency checks, consumer compatibility, current-use evaluation and a v2 subset migration. It is finite and works on trusted, interpreted JSON input.

records.title: Revision of Knowledge, Versions and Acceptance of Norms
records.titleRu: Пересмотр знания, версии и принятие норм
records.summary: The paper sets rules for changing knowledge, its grounds, norms and chosen representations, connecting them with history, publication and current admission. A finite revision model passed 73 checks with fixed inputs (0 failed); three model defects were found and fixed during preparation. In one observation of a file operation, a separate copy failed finalisation in a previous update (301 of 302 save operations succeeded) and the service gave no cause; the full archive still matched the canonical sources (348 of 348 hashes). No real distributed backend, authentication, books or classifier were used, and 36 subject and load setups remain planned and not executed. Superiority over simply replacing the last record is not shown.

records.title: Evaluation, Counterexamples and the Limits of Claims
records.summary: The paper proposes a programme for testing meaning management as a whole process, from request to observable result and back-tracing. The scientific question is whether explicit meaning objects, conditions, dependencies and provenance help a person or a model reach a better-grounded result under limited source access and budget. The question is not answered on a representative or independent load: local targeted comparisons against a strong flat implementation gave equal statuses and no established superiority. An appendix keeps runs R37-R44, including first failures.

records.title: Knowledge Compilation: Preparing Results and the Admissibility of Reuse
records.titleRu: Компиляция знания: подготовка результатов и допустимость повторного использования
records.summary: The paper treats reuse of prepared results of extraction, retrieval, composition and professional preparation as a separate admission operation. Reusing a prepared result requires a match with the new request, current constraints, required grounds and the recipient's profile. The paper formalises this boundary and states conditional properties, an economic formulation, strong alternatives and grounds for refutation. The outcome is a research model and a finite executable profile. Effectiveness on real books, causal usefulness and industrial correctness remain hypotheses. The one measured efficiency result, a local paired pilot, found no stable gain.

records.title: Knowledge Utility, the Cost of Meaning Artifacts and Resource Management
records.titleRu: Полезность знаний, стоимость смысловых артефактов и управление ресурсами
records.summary: The paper proposes a way to link the life cycle of meaning artifacts to observed resource use, conditions of application and results for specific recipients. The object of evaluation is not a universal "value of a text" but the contribution of an artifact version to a goal fixed in advance, relative to an explicit alternative. Costs, including those of the evaluation itself, are counted. The paper offers a synthesis and a contract profile, not a value theory. No retention or ranking policy based on conditional utility has been tested on a real load; the appendix holds only local resource observations from runs R38-R44.

records.title: Registry of Shared Artifacts: Identity, Fields and Obligations
records.titleRu: Реестр общих артефактов: идентичность, поля и обязанности
records.summary: This specification defines a registry of shared artifact types for the Meaning Management model. Registry version 0.1 lists 34 conceptual types: 30 introduced earlier and four added explicitly. A common envelope, `mm-envelope/0.1`, makes an addressable, immutable revision, and profiles set the requirements for each kind of record. The text separates five levels of representation, from artifact type down to physical placement, and defines a four-state value for known, unknown, not-applicable and withheld fields. It declares itself a concept draft that develops toward the draft Knowledge Contract v3 (`3.0.0-draft.1`), and it does not announce a ready API or a completed v3 schema.

records.title: Identity, Dependencies and Invalidation
records.summary: This specification sets out how a stored, derived result is addressed, found as a candidate, revised when its basis changes, and admitted for a new delivery. It separates payload identity, build identity, lookup identity and a mutable current head, and treats byte equality, recipe equality, meaning compatibility, sufficiency for a request and authority to deliver as different relations. It also covers negative and top-k results, change events, late workers and restore. The result is a research specification with a finite executable profile; the text states that a real distributed system is not yet implemented.

records.title: Compiled Artifact Contract
records.summary: This specification defines `CompiledArtifact`, a stored derived result of a declared extraction, selection, transformation or assembly of knowledge. It links the result to its representation, build recipe, dependencies, requirements and evidence, so that people and agents can reuse it under stated conditions. It defines a bounded profile, `i16-compiled-artifact/0.1`, with a published JSON Schema and a finite checking program. It adds no new type to the shared registry. The text calls itself a research specification and says the schema and program are not an industrial service or a universal solver of meaning.

records.title: ContextPackage: Specification and Bounded Executable Profile
records.titleRu: ContextPackage: спецификация и ограниченный исполнимый профиль
records.summary: This specification defines `ContextPackage`, a versioned package of statements and conditions prepared for one intent and one bounded use. It lets a reader check provenance, coverage, dependencies, scope of applicability and budget. The text lists 13 groups of required fields, a coverage vocabulary, a separate stop-reason vocabulary, and budget and validation rules. It states that it keeps the status of a research proposal. A bounded profile, `i14-context-package/0.1`, defines a finite serialisation, a local recipient and a validator. Successful validation grants no authority to act and does not confirm physical execution.

records.title: Family of Contracts for Operations on Meanings and Knowledge
records.titleRu: Семейство контрактов операций над смыслами и знаниями
records.summary: This specification defines a family of contracts that tie knowledge to the actions allowed on it: preserving a source, extracting meaning, aligning an illustration with text, retrieving, preparing bounded context, handing it over, explaining, doing work, revising and reusing a result. A contract states under which inputs and conditions an operation is admissible, what it keeps and changes, which outcomes are allowed and how they are confirmed. The text defines 17 operation profiles and five outcomes. It declares itself a concept draft (edition 0.9) aligned with the draft Knowledge Contract v3.

records.title: Knowledge Contract v3: Synthesis Specification
records.summary: This specification defines a target design for Knowledge Contract v3 (target identifier `3.0.0-draft.1`): a versioned, bounded package of meaning content for a declared purpose of use. It links typed content to requirements, scope, sources, dependencies, preservation obligations and observations. The text describes nine logical groups, six selective profiles, separate validation levels, and a limited migration of a six-field legacy subset. A concrete carrier, `kc-synthesis/0.1`, is covered only within its own stated scope.

records.title: Knowledge Bases and Contract Evolution
records.titleRu: Версии оснований знания и эволюция контрактов
records.summary: This specification states a requirement for recording which versions of contracts, profiles and rules a knowledge or decision card was created under, and for handling later change. A card keeps the exact versions used at creation; checks against newer rules are recorded separately, and provenance and earlier revisions are never rewritten. The text defines version layers, creation and change records, an impact graph, a review process and a proposed metadata profile with a local validator. It states that the contract family does not yet have approved production schemas, so the document sets requirements and a bounded profile only.

records.title: Policy for Permissible Reuse
records.summary: This specification (version 1.0) defines a temporal policy for when a previously prepared knowledge result may be reused. The policy is relative to a concrete request, recipient, artifact revision and accepted rule version. It names three time modes (`strict_current`, `historical_pinned`, `bounded_stale`), defines soft and hard deadlines computed from the last sufficient check, and sets a priority order in which prohibitions and current access come before cost savings. The evidence status is stated as a proposed policy with a bounded executable profile.

records.title: Content Types and Independent Classification Axes
records.titleRu: Типы содержания и независимые оси классификации
records.summary: This specification (version 0.7) proposes how to keep apart the differences that matter for search, explanation, document preparation, visual comparison and work execution. It offers ten analytical axes, eight canonical facets of a `MeaningObject`, and a profile for multimodal content. It keeps the 34 general artifact types and the `mm-envelope/0.1` envelope from the artifact registry, and does not add new general types. Practical scope is text and images; audio and video are described only in theory. The text calls the result a working model open to checking and revision.

records.title: Independent Statuses, Assessment Scopes and Transitions
records.titleRu: Независимые статусы, области оценки и переходы
records.summary: This specification (model version `status-model/0.1`) argues that a single global label such as "ready", "valid" or "reliable" is insufficient, because it mixes presence of data, semantic support, execution, external effects, currency and scientific status. It introduces 22 independent axes with addressable observations and rules for change, and describes several of them: coverage of a request, run phase and outcome, stop reason, effect observation, check result, research status, case status and data origin. The text calls itself a design model, not a ready industrial schema.
